Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not

From J. Littlemore, CLWYD

Thanks for OUTLET 101: my first.
I am very impressed by it and
also saddened by your comments
in the editorial re +3 disks. I
hope you can obtain more before
your six months supply runs out.
I have ordered up to August,hop-
ing I can send for more later. I
have also ordered some back num-
bers and the OUTLET EXTRA 1.

I have had a 48K Spectrum since
1984 - obtained from a workmate
who had bought it for his son
who, after about 3 or 4 months,
didn't bother with it as one of
his mates had a Commodore and he
preferred that to his own.It was
as good as new with some games
and a joystick.

I use my Spectrum with Tasword
II to keep files on my hobby. I
also have ADDRESS MANAGER from
OCP & a lot of friends in conn-
ection with my hobby. I used to
buy S.U. & Y.S. Mags & copied
programs from them.

Just over a year ago I saw a +3
disk drive 128K on a 2nd-hand
market stall and on making
enquiries it was very cheap so I
bought it. I was given 5 games
disks and a lightgun. The stall-
holder said that as far as he
knew it was in working order.

There was no manual with it but
I found an advert in Format that
I had just started to receive so
sent for it.


I set it up as instructed to
find out that it would only work
on cassette tape and not disk. I
remembered reading in one of the
mags about a built-in test for
the +3 so I looked through and
found it and,on carrying out the
test, everything worked except
the disk drive which indicated
too slow, so I decided to look
inside and found that the belt
(a flat neoprene belt) was slip-
ping.


So, I removed the drive and belt
then I measured its circumfer-
ence and found a rubber band
just a bit smaller and fitted
it. I then replaced the drive
and it now works OK.


I have copied a lot of programs
from tape to disk, as well as
Tasword II  (with a conversion
from the same mag as the test
for the +3). I have copied all
my files as well as making new
ones to disk - it is much faster
to save and load.

I note from OUTLET 101 the
article about +3 disk-slipping;
also the address for new drive
belts. I will be ordering a
couple of these as my rubber
band will give in eventually.

ADDRESS MANAGER will not work on
the +3 - even in 48K.

                J. Littlemore


Brian Cavers to J. Littlemore

I think that belt slippage on
the +3 drives could be quite
common. I'd be very pleased if
you could write an article for
OUTLET describing a simple blow
by blow account of how to change
the belt - a sort of idiot's
guide. This is the kind of thing
that is a piece of cake to one
person but rather daunting to
another unless they have very
precise directions.

This is just what OUTLET is for
- sharing ones knowledge with
each other. I think there could
well be a few users who might
get their +3 drive working again
from such info.
                   Brian

From Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Ron and Brian,

Having accumulated a number of
padded envelopes in which the
issues are now being sent I
wondered if it would be any help
to you if they were returned for
re-use. It would obviously be a
saving in not having to buy new
envelopes and no problem stick-
ing the current label over the
old so no need to keep sorted as
to which goes to who. The down
side could be the time taken to
cover an old stamp and post mark
plus having to find a way of
re-glueing the flap.  Obviously
envelopes with torn flaps would
not be much good.


When considering changing a
printer from serial to parallel
due to a change of computer or
acquiring a +D, the situation
could be resolved instead by
acquiring a parallel to serial
converter that simply fits in
series with the printer lead. I
have seen such devices for about
`10 or `15 at computer shows.

They can be obtained in a varie-
ty of forms, S - P, P - S, to do
both and with or without a print
buffer of various capacities.
Some can have the options swit-
ched from software.Obviously the
more facilities the more expens-
ive, generally ! I have used one
to run my parallel printer from
the serial port of the 128.


Peritel, Euroconnector and SCART
are different names for the same
signal standards and, in some
cases, the same type of connect-
or. The SCART standard defines
signal levels, type of connector
and which pin does what. Some
makers decide to call this a
Euroconnector. A non DIN conn-
ector cannot obviously be called
SCART so Peritel would indicate
the signal standards it is prov-
iding.


The +2a and +3 has RGB generated
directly by the ULA which goes
to the RGB outputs and is also
split off to an IC that takes
RGB and converts it to PAL comp-
osite video for the modulator.


However,the 48K ULA provides R-Y
B-Y, and chroma (Y,U,V) signals.
These then use an IC to generate
PAL comp. video. There is no RGB
as such available within the 48K
circuitry. It should be possible
to tap off the R-Y, B-Y and
chroma and use such as a TDA2530
or AN5612 IC with associated
circuitry to generate RGB.

There was at one time a device
available that went onto the
expansion port of the 48K where
Y,U,V signals are shown avail-
able (Video is also shown but
some models had a link missing)
and gave RGB but I have not seen
one for many years and have no
idea how they performed but I do
remember being told they tended
to "blow up" Spectrums. Whether

due to a fault in design or the
more common action of connecting
or removing either accidentally
or deliberately while powered I
have no idea.

Regarding the lightgun query I
would assume they work on simil-
ar lines to the light pen except
it has a lens system to focus
the TV screen scanning spot onto
a detector so is used a distance
away. Some while ago in Issue 50
I did some notes (Outclass) with
a BASIC/MC routine to experiment
with a light pen. I would guess
similar idea would work with the
gun by using the appropriate in-
put port to be read.Which socket
does the gun plug into? I never
used one but believe it has the
RS232/keypad type connector.

Perhaps comparing general form
of my code with that of the gun
routine may help to track down
the relevant section of code.

Referring back to the routine in
#50 it obviously will not do
anything without an appropriate
pen connected. A few additional
notes may be of interest. It has
4 sections. A MC routine to det-
ect an input from the pen and
also a timer which starts when
the line scan is at the top of
the screen.It returns a value in
x which is related to the verti-
cal position on screen.This val-
ue which is fixed by the given
point in the calibrate screen is
used as a fixed reference (vari-
able REF).


RUN 1 in the PEN TEST program in
Issue 50 shows the aforemention-
ed screen.

Lines 1000 - 2000 produce an
example of a vertical menu.
RUN 1000 for this screen.


RUN 3000 is a method for an
alternative way where the menu
is horizontal at bottom of
screen. In this case x relates
to the time it takes the moving
square to travel across screen.


Lines at 5000 detect if the pen
is not receiving an input signal
and to hold the program in a
pause until it does.


Regarding disks and drives, Ron
and Brian may be interested (and
pleased) to know that I use an
OUTLET disc that has been form-
atted on their drives as a
"standard" when aligning disc
drives. Working on the basis
that if their discs work on the
majority of readers drives they
must be somewhere near a "stand-
ard".


Having set up a number of drives
that were rejected as refusing
to load, damaged in the post and
etc - from such discs I do not
recall having any problems read-
ing discs from a number of other
drives. Either my own numerous
collection or other owners.


I do not bother to use sophisti-
cated test equiptment when sett-
ing up a drive but simply use
trial and error with a short
LOAD @ loop with error trapping
and adjust the head position -
firstly to ensure it finds T0
reliably then various tracks
across disc. I carefully move
either way and find the posit-
ions at which it just fails. I
then reset back to the mid posi-
tion.


The final test is a gruelling 10
minute run with a loop setting T
& S at random and repeated saves
and loads soon show up any
problems due to wear or sticking
head movement.


I have some 100 issues of Outlet
on 3.5" disc and as far as I
recall have not had any problems
loading except for an odd item
on perhaps two discs. No, the
drives used mainly to read
Outlet have not been set up from
Outlet discs - they are "as
original" when obtained. Errors
are more likely to be due to
below-par discs with a bad sec-
tor than drives. I have only had
two damaged in the post and
again suspect this damage was
due to a faulty disc in that it
looked as if the two halves of
the case had not been properly
put together rather than actual
physical breakage. Lets hope I
have not pushed my luck saying
this.


Let me end on a frivolous note.
Did you know the 3D spectacles
for the TV 3D experiment some
while back often work well on
computer moving demo screens?


The method gives varying degree
of 3D from very good to poor
depending on the screen content
and most of all how it is
moving. It must be from side to
side, the faster the movement of
one part compared with the other
parts increases the 3D depth
effect.

Direction of movement will also
dictate if the spectacles are
used correctly or used the wrong
way round.


You do not have 3D specs? (the
type with one lens darker then
the other - not the red/green
sort). If not then try making
your own with smoked/brown/grey
toffee paper over one eye. It
seems one eye needs to be
restricted to about half the
brightness of the other. The
brain then gets confused (I do
not need toffee papers for
that!) as it takes longer to
process a darker image in one
eye than the bright image in the
other. When the brain receives
two images almost the same (from
slightly different viewpoints)
but at different times it tries
to make sense and decides one
part is further away than the
other.


This type of 3D can make you
quite giddy because the image
must be continually moving
across the screen so the camera
has to keep panning round and
round if the scene does not have
objects moving at different rel-
ative speeds.

                  Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

I'm not sure it's worth the ex-
pense of a special posting to
return padded envelopes but it
could be helpful to return odd
ones as and when writing anyway,
ie, if they can be slipped in
without extra cost.

Thanks for all the info - those
moving 3D pictures are fascinat-
ing aren't they and work with
any picture so long as it is
panning or an object is moving
horizontally. However, as you
say, it is ultimately merely of
scientific interest because the
constant motion necessary could
hardly be sustained for long;
imagine News at Ten with the
newsreader on a swing!   Brian

From JOHN CLEVELAND - LONDON






Dear Ron and Brian,

Concerning Fred Ridout's diffi-
culty transferring Art Studio to
+3 disk (Outletters 102), I sus-
pect the root of the problem is
simply that his version of Art
Studio is 128K whereas the conv-
ersion program ARTODISK (Outlet
101) seems to be designed speci-
fically for the 48K version, as
evidenced by the opening prompt
which reads:"Start your original
Art Studio 48K tape".


I referred briefly last month to
Graham Collier's"ARTFULLY DODGY"
utility for converting 128K Art
Studio to +3 disc. It is obtain-
able by sending a formatted disk
and sae to:
          Fountain PD,
         11 Camel Road,
         London E16 2DE
      (Tel. 0171 476 5915)

Not having the 128K tape, I am
unable to test this program,
though I note from the on-screen
instructions that "All saves and
loads by Art Studio will still
be to or from tape or micro-
drive". This is a significant
disadvantage compared to ARTO-
DISK which provides direct acc-
ess to drives A and M, and even
an external B-drive.

Concerning Peter Johnson's query
last month about how to make
Wordmaster default to disc rath-
er than tape, I suggest the fol-
lowing alternative approaches:

(a) Try loading Wordmaster, set
the drive you want,exit to Basic
and re-SAVE the Wordmaster CODE
file(s).

(b) Try POKEing address 63347,
which holds the drive number and
or address 63571 which holds the
CODE of the drive number displ-
ayed in the file-handling menu
(eg, 48 for Drive 0).These addr-
esses apply to the microdrive/
tape version of Wordmaster, and
also to the +3 version (in which
63347 holds 0,1,2,3 for Drives
T,A,B and M respectively.

63571 holds the CODE of the dis-
played drive LETTER). I presume
the +D version is similar though
I don't have a copy to test.

Incidentally, the corresponding
addresses in the SAM version of
Wordmaster are 96115 and 96339.
You can insert DEVICE d(PEEK
96339-48)in line 15 of the Basic
to gain access to any drive
whose number (+48) is POKEd into
96339. For example, to access a
Masterdos ramdisk, one could
further modify the Basic so that
entering "3" at the ERASE prompt
causes a POKE 96339,51 followed
by GOTO 10 to return to the file
handling menu which will now
show Drive 3 selected. And of
course, DIR 1 in line 50 should
be changed to DIR *.

Is there an update of Michael
Atkins' OUTLETTERS database that
appeared under the filename...
'OUTLET.MF3' in Outlet 78 (+3
Addenders)?

         All the best,

        John Cleveland


Brian Cavers to John Cleveland



Many thanks, John.

Fred Ridout loaned me his copy
of Art Studio 128K and I tried
the ARTFULLY DODGY software you
sent me - but without success.

After a great deal of trouble I
did eventually get ART STUDIO on
to +3 disk but almost all its
features crashed and it was un-
usable. I could draw nothing.
About the only thing I could
access was to change the border
and ink colours etc! Oh and fill
worked as well but I had nothing
to fill except the screen!


The problem may possibly be due
to the missing files you mention
(STUDIO and STUDIO1). I found
these files were included on the
original ART STUDIO tape but
needed some slight changes. This
I did and got the thing running
but possibly there should be
other changes to them.

By chance I found I HAD got a
copy of the early 48K version of
ART STUDIO  together with the
dreaded LENSLOCK. This tape was
amongst some unused game tapes I
had received in a bundle of
stuff when I bought a secondhand
+3 - and I had never really took
much notice of it. However, it
failed also to transfer to +3
with either DODGY or ARTODISK.


To be honest I am heartily sick
of the whole thing! I spent many
hours fiddling with tapes and
all to no avail. Both ARTODISK
and DODGY have instructions that
is not as clear as they should
be. Re-reading ARTODISK it seems
to be for the +2 128K version
and yet, as you say, elsewhere
refers only to the 48K version.


I consider myself fairly au fait
with things 'Spectrumese' yet
even with both 48K and 128K ver-
sions of ART STUDIO and TWO
different tape-to-+3-disk conv-
ertors I still ended up with
nothing at all that would work!
A novice would have little hope,
I feel.


If anyone else can conjure succ-
ess from any of these programs
then please write to us.

Thanks for the WORDMASTER info
and the MF+3 databases which I
will drop in the +3 issue as and
when there is room.I regret that
there is no update to the MF+3
file that Michael Atkins sent us
but if Michael has added to the
file perhaps he will send it in
when he sees this letter!

                         Brian.

From W.T. Buxton, CHESHIRE


Dear Brian,

I have just received ORBIT Issue
No.102 and I note that you
discuss 'Peritel' connections as
shown on Page 25 of OUTLETTERS
and which are also shown in
Chapter 10 in the +3 handbook
under the heading of VDU monit-
or.

I have come in possession of a
TA monochrom monitor which has a
15-pin D-shell connector for
plugging directly to a PC. I en-
close a photocopy of the funct-
ion of the 15 pins with the mon-
itor's technical specification.


I would now like to have a short
cable made consisting of a
15-pin D-shell socket at one end
and an 8-pin DIN plug at the
other to plug in to the RGB/
PERITEL socket of my Spectrum
+3. This will readily enable me
to use the monitor again for PC
purposes and avoid having to
make any connections inside the
monitor. I can solder and use a
screwdriver but I am no electr-
ician!

Question 1:  Is this possible
with this monitor and a Spectrum
+3?

Question 2:  Which pins require
connecting with which? Have you
a sketch?


I would really appreciate your
advice as having passed 70 my
eyesight is not improving and I
feel the clarity of a monitor
would help me greatly. Because I
am so keen to know about this
possibility I am enclosing an
SAE in the hope that I will not
have to wait until the next
issue of ORBIT! I hope I am not
being too presumptious!

       Yours faithfully,

          Bill Buxton


Brian Cavers to Bill Buxton

You should,by now, have received
Ron's acknowledgement of your
letter explaining why we are not
able to answer queries privately
but only publicly through OUTLET
in these letters pages.This also
helps others who may have the
very same problem!

Yours is a case where another
OUTLET reader may be able to
help YOU! For my part (I'm not a
'hardware' man). Referring to
Peter Johnson's DRIVECHATs in
OUTLET 89 and 90,I get the impr-
ession it is perfectly possible
to connect a +3 to a mono PC
monitor but it might need extra
circuitry and not just a lead.


I will print here the pinouts of
your monitor and hopefully Peter
or Malcolm Perry who is another
genius with these things, may be
able to advise...

  1 Reserved
  2 Video
  3 Reserved
  4 Reserved
  5 Self-test input
  6 Reserved
  7 Video Return
  8 Reserved
  9 Reserved
 10 Ground
 11 Reserved(monitor sense open)
 12 Monitor sense ground
 13 H.SYNC
 14 V.SYNC
 15 Reserved


There are two other contacts you
can try...

     MEEDSMORE DISTRIBUTION
 28 FARRIERS WAY INDUSTRIAL EST.
 NETHERTON, MERSEYSIDE, L30 4XL
       TEL: 0151 521 2202

             and...

    VIDEO AND COMPUTER WORLD
         48 DUKE STREET
           COLDSTREAM
            SCOTLAND
       TEL: 01890 883232

I'm told Meedsmore can make up
any lead and Video and Computer
World have all kinds of Sinclair
leads in stock. I recommend you
ring Meedsmore and give them the
details.

Incidentally, Peter Johnson's
address is Saddle Hill Road,No.1
R.D., Dunedin, New Zealand and
his DRIVECHAT in Issue 90 does
invite readers to write to him.

If you do get it working OK then
please let us know, and how, so
others can benefit.

                          Brian


From George B. Munro, LONDON,NW3




Dear Brian,

My reason for writing is to ten-
tatively make a suggestion with
regard to the program NAPOLEON
in last month's OUTLET. In its
present form it is almost imp-
ossible to complete thus giving
lots of frustration but little
or no enjoyment - not, I would
have thought, the real purpose
of a 'game'. Despite having said
this, I did (as yu will see from
the enclosed) manage to complete
it - more by good luck than good
judgement.


My suggestion would be as shown
below...

3010 GO SUB 7000 : IF round = 5
     THEN etc

3020 PRINT AT 20,0; "You have "
 + ("two rounds" AND round =1) +
 ("one round" AND round = 2) + "
 to try again":LET round=round+1
 : PRINT AT 18,8;"ROUNDS PLAYED"
 ; round-1

This would not greatly change
the game but it would slightly
alter the odds which at the
moment, as the program stands,
are in my opinion astronomic.

         Yours as ever,

        George B. Munro


Brian Cavers to George Munro

I certainly agree that the purp-
ose of a game is to entertain.It
is an art though to find just
the right degree of difficulty -
too easy and there is no chall-
enge - too hard and it is just
frustrating.

I well remember an arcade game
with fantastic graphics in which
you start off driving a jeep
while all around you are tanks
and so on trying to blow you to
kingdom come. I tried this game
three times and each time I
survived SEVEN seconds! Not bad
value for a `9.99 game. I guess
that's about 37p a second for 27
seconds.
                       Brian.

I do not bother to use sophisti- cated test equiptment when sett- ing up a drive but simply use trial and error with a short LOAD @ loop with error trapping and adjust the head position - firstly to ensure it finds T0 reliably then various tracks across disc. I carefully move either way and find the posit- ions at which it just fails. I then reset back to the mid posi- tion.

The final test is a gruelling 10 minute run with a loop setting T & S at random and repeated saves and loads soon show up any problems due to wear or sticking head movement.

I have some 100 issues of Outlet on 3.5" disc and as far as I recall have not had any problems loading except for an odd item on perhaps two discs. No, the drives used mainly to read Outlet have not been set up from Outlet discs - they are "as original" when obtained. Errors are more likely to be due to below-par discs with a bad sec- tor than drives. I have only had two damaged in the post and again suspect this damage was due to a faulty disc in that it looked as if the two halves of the case had not been properly put together rather than actual physical breakage. Lets hope I have not pushed my luck saying this.

Let me end on a frivolous note. Did you know the 3D spectacles for the TV 3D experiment some while back often work well on computer moving demo screens?

The method gives varying degree of 3D from very good to poor depending on the screen content and most of all how it is moving. It must be from side to side, the faster the movement of one part compared with the other parts increases the 3D depth effect.

Direction of movement will also dictate if the spectacles are used correctly or used the wrong way round.

You do not have 3D specs? (the type with one lens darker then the other - not the red/green sort). If not then try making your own with smoked/brown/grey toffee paper over one eye. It seems one eye needs to be restricted to about half the brightness of the other. The brain then gets confused (I do not need toffee papers for that!) as it takes longer to process a darker image in one eye than the bright image in the other. When the brain receives two images almost the same (from slightly different viewpoints) but at different times it tries to make sense and decides one part is further away than the other.

This type of 3D can make you quite giddy because the image must be continually moving across the screen so the camera has to keep panning round and round if the scene does not have objects moving at different rel- ative speeds.

Malcolm Perry

### От Malcolm Perry, KIDDERMINSTER

Дорогие Ron и Brian,

Накопив изрядное количество пупырчатых конвертов, в которых вы теперь рассылаете номера, я подумал: может, вам пригодится, если я верну их для повторного использования? Естественно, конверты с разорванными клапанами в дело уже не пойдут.

Если вы задумываетесь о замене принтера с последовательного на параллельный из-за смены компьютера или приобретения +D, эту проблему можно решить иначе: купить преобразователь параллельного интерфейса в последовательный (parallel to serial converter), который просто включается в разрыв кабеля принтера. Я видел такие устройства по цене около £10 или £15 на компьютерных выставках.

Они бывают самых разных видов: S - P (serial to parallel), P - S (parallel to serial), двунаправленные, а также со встроенным буфером печати разного объема или без него. В некоторых параметры переключаются программно. Естественно, чем больше возможностей, тем, как правило, дороже! Я использовал такой, чтобы подключить свой параллельный принтер к последовательному порту модели 128.

Peritel, Euroconnector и SCART — это разные названия одних и тех же стандартов сигналов и, в некоторых случаях, одного и того же типа разъема. Стандарт SCART определяет уровни сигналов, тип разъема и распиновку. Некоторые производители предпочитают называть его Euroconnector. Разъем, отличный от SCART (например, DIN), очевидно, нельзя назвать SCART, поэтому обозначение Peritel указывает на то, каким стандартам сигналов он соответствует.

В моделях +2a и +3 сигналы RGB формируются непосредственно внутри ULA. Они идут на выходы RGB, а также параллельно поступают на микросхему, которая берет RGB и преобразует его в полный цветной телевизионный сигнал стандарта PAL (composite video) для модулятора.

Однако в 48K микросхема ULA выдает сигналы цветоразностные R-Y, B-Y и яркостной/цветовой сигнал (Y,U,V). Затем с помощью отдельной ИМС из них формируется композитный сигнал PAL. Сигналов RGB как таковых в схеме 48K просто нет. Должна быть возможность снять сигналы R-Y, B-Y и яркость/цветность и использовать микросхему вроде TDA2530 или AN5612 с соответствующей обвязкой для формирования RGB.

В свое время выпускалось устройство, подключавшееся к системному разъему 48K, где разведены сигналы Y,U,V (видеосигнал там тоже обозначен, но на некоторых моделях отсутствовала перемычка), и выдававшее RGB. Однако я не видел их уже много лет и не имею понятия, как они работали на практике. Помню только, что поговаривали, будто они частенько «сжигали» Спектрумы. Было ли это связано с ошибкой в конструкции или же с более банальным подключением/отключением устройства при включенном питании (случайно или намеренно) — я не знаю.

Что касается вопроса о световом пистолете, я полагаю, что они работают по тому же принципу, что и световое перо, за исключением того, что в пистолете есть оптическая система линз, фокусирующая бегущий по экрану телевизора луч на датчик, благодаря чему его можно использовать на расстоянии. Некоторое время назад в выпуске №50 я опубликовал заметки (рубрика Outclass) с процедурой на BASIC/MC для экспериментов со световым пером. Думаю, аналогичная идея сработает и с пистолетом, если считывать данные из соответствующего входного порта. В какой разъем втыкается пистолет? Я им никогда не пользовался, но полагаю, что там разъем типа RS232/keypad.

Возможно, сопоставление общей структуры моего кода с процедурой для пистолета поможет отыскать нужный участок программы.

Возвращаясь к процедуре из №50: понятно, что без подключенного пера она ничего делать не будет. Пара дополнительных замечаний может оказаться полезной. В ней 4 части: процедура в машинных кодах для обнаружения входного сигнала с пера, а также таймер, который запускается в тот момент, когда строчная развертка находится в верхней части экрана. Она возвращает значение в переменной x, которое связано с вертикальным положением на экране. Это значение, привязанное к определенной точке на экране калибровки, используется в качестве фиксированного ориентира (переменная REF).

Команда RUN 1 в программе PEN TEST из выпуска №50 отображает вышеупомянутый экран.

Строки 1000–2000 создают пример вертикального меню. Чтобы увидеть этот экран, введите RUN 1000.

RUN 3000 — альтернативный вариант, где меню расположено горизонтально в нижней части экрана. В этом случае переменная x связана со временем, которое требуется движущемуся квадрату для перемещения по экрану.
